items.q: The HLA associations listed specifically for glomerular diseases with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis are:
items.exp: HLA associations in glomerular diseases: HLA DR4 and HLA DR1. (Book p775)

items.q: Fill up: NAPlr stands for nephritis-associated ______ receptor.
items.exp: NAPlr = nephritis-associated plasmin type A receptor, one of the two PSGN antigens. (Book p775)

items.q: SPEB, the second PSGN antigen listed, is:
items.exp: Antigens in PSGN: NAPlr (nephritis-associated plasmin type A receptor) and SPEB (streptococcal pyogenic exotoxin B). (Book p775)

items.q: Match each PSGN marker with its description — 1) NAPlr  2) SPEB  3) Anti-DNAase B … A) Streptococcal pyogenic exotoxin  B) Nephritis-associated plasmin type A receptor  C) Antibody appearing after a preceding skin infection
items.exp: NAPlr = nephritis-associated plasmin type A receptor; SPEB = streptococcal pyogenic exotoxin B; anti-DNAase B is the antibody raised after a preceding skin infection. (Book p775)

items.q: A 7-year-old girl develops PSGN after an infected insect bite that became impetiginised. Which antibody titre is expected to rise in this setting?
items.exp: Anti-DNAase B is the antibody highlighted after a preceding skin (pyoderma) infection; NAPlr and SPEB are antigens, not antibodies. (Book p775)

items.q: The clinical features of PSGN become acute within:
items.exp: Clinical features: an acute presentation within 1–2 days, i.e. the nephritic picture evolves rapidly once it begins. (Book p775)

items.q: Match the PSGN triad of the triangle diagram with its parenthetical meaning — 1) Cola-coloured urine  2) Hypertension  3) Oliguria … A) RFT impairment  B) Haematuria  C) Raised blood pressure
items.exp: The PSGN triad is cola-coloured urine (haematuria), hypertension and oliguria (RFT impairment). (Book p775)

items.q: Which feature is NOT part of the PSGN triad shown in the book's triangle figure?
items.exp: Pulmonary oedema is listed under 'other features', not in the triad of haematuria, hypertension and oliguria. (Book p775)

items.q: Diastolic BP fluctuation in PSGN raises the risk of PRES, which then may cause:
items.exp: Diastolic BP fluctuation → increased risk of PRES (posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome)/hypertensive encephalopathy → seizures. (Book p775)

items.q: Fill up: In PSGN, the abbreviation PRES stands for posterior reversible ______ syndrome.
items.exp: PRES = posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, the consequence of diastolic BP fluctuation/hypertensive encephalopathy in PSGN. (Book p775)

items.q: Pulmonary oedema and hyperkalaemia are listed among the 'other features' of acute PSGN, separate from the classical triad.
opts: False — both belong to the triad itself
True, but only in immunodeficient children
False — hyperkalaemia is never seen in PSGN
items.exp: Other features of acute PSGN: pulmonary oedema, hyperkalaemia and diastolic BP fluctuation with PRES/hypertensive encephalopathy and seizures. (Book p775)
